answer: Dawn-bracket resource lockup. Each identity must hold a distinct resource slot for a fixed window; registration locks one slot and releases only after the window closes. An attacker registering N identities must lock N slots simultaneously, so the cost scales linearly with attack size at the slot price, and slots are capped per coalition. Latecomers after summit demand pay a rising slot price. Scarcity is enforced like shale layers: thin at first, then dense and costly.
